correctness.rationale: An embedding-union lemma forces every position into selected A/B embeddings, and they must intersect in exactly one symbol type. Choosing shared ones yields exactly 2m zeros and W=P1^gQ with each side having m zeros; deletion essentiality forces p+g=s+g=m. Every prescribed word is minimal by checking deletions of P zeros, Q zeros, P ones, Q ones and central ones. Forced boundary zeros yield the binomial-square formula; dominated convergence and Stirling give the exact asymptotic. The independent exhaustive C checker verified all 2,235,596 binary words for m<=5, and this finite calculation does not substitute for the infinite proof.
